question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{x+1}-1.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{x+1}-1,$ and simplify:

$$
\eqalign{
		\dfrac {x} {\sqrt{x+1}+1} &= \[5pt]
		\dfrac {x} {\sqrt{x+1}+1}\cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{x+1}-1}{\sqrt{x+1}-1} &= \[5pt]
		\dfrac {x(\sqrt{x+1}-1)} {(\sqrt{x+1}+1)(\sqrt{x+1}-1)} &= \[5pt]
                \dfrac {x(\sqrt{x+1}-1)} {(\sqrt{x+1})^2-1^2} &= \[5pt]
                \dfrac {x(\sqrt{x+1}-1)} {x+1-1} &= \[5pt]
                \dfrac {x(\sqrt{x+1}-1)} {x}&=\[5pt]
\sqrt{x+1}-1
	}
$$
